rationale_overall: No genuine catalyst this week rose to swap-worthy strength. Nuclear coverage (USAF C-17 microreactor airlift to Utah, Wisconsin PSC site search, Florida nuclear policy chatter) reinforces the existing SMR thesis but names no new investable ticker. Rocket Lab and Nvidia both drew only generic think-piece coverage (Fool.com 'Nvidia vs AMD', 'Where Will Rocket Lab Stock Be in 10 Years') rather than a fresh catalyst, so both are kept as-is. Filtered as noise: foreign/non-US-listed items (Ariane 6/ESA Celeste, UAE hybrid rocket test, China Spring Festival robotics showcase, India S-400/fighter-jet program, Turkey warship denial), private/non-tradable entities (SpaceX Starship test, Deep Space Energy lunar reactor funding), illiquid penny-stock newswire uranium-claim press releases (Terra Clean, Auric Minerals), local/generic listicle content (robotics-club competitions, 'Best Robotics Stocks to Research' roundup, Texas AI data-center puff piece), a stale mis-dated 2018 arms-control article, and recurring NASA Artemis II delay coverage which is not a tradable single-name catalyst. Watchlist composition (GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, SMR plus anchor SPY) stands unchanged this period.
